package_info.why_malicious: The package was crafted to exploit a ZIP Slip (path traversal) vulnerability in the CDNJS automated ingestion pipeline, allowing arbitrary file write and potential remote code execution on the CDN infrastructure. This could lead to compromise of the CDN, exfiltration of secret keys, and tampering with any library served by CDNJS.

execution_context.trigger: package ingestion (automated bot fetch from npm)

malicious_snippets.code_language: shell (filesystem path traversal via tarball structure)
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: During package ingestion, the tarball contains files with directory traversal sequences in their paths, causing the extraction process to write files outside the intended directory, potentially overwriting sensitive files or placing malicious scripts on the server.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The use of directory traversal sequences in archive file paths is a classic exploit technique (ZIP Slip) to escape the intended extraction directory and write files to arbitrary locations on the server.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal npm packages should only contain files within their own directory structure; files should never be extracted outside the package root.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: There is no legitimate reason for a package to include files with directory traversal in their paths.
key_indicators: Presence of '../' or similar traversal in archive file paths
Files extracted to /tmp or other system directories from package tarball

required_permissions: potentially environment_vars if script is executed

malicious_snippets.code_snippet:
Hello there, I'm RyotaK ;) (Doing some security tests now)
Retesting
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: If executed, the script simply outputs benign text, but a real attacker could use this vector to execute arbitrary code, exfiltrate secrets, or modify system state.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The ability to place and potentially execute arbitrary scripts on the server is a critical security risk, even if the PoC script is benign.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: No package should be able to place executable files outside its own directory, nor should arbitrary scripts be executed as part of package ingestion.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: None; package ingestion should never execute or place arbitrary scripts outside the package scope.
key_indicators: Unexpected shell scripts written to /tmp or other system locations
Scripts containing test or exfiltration logic

attack_chain.action: Attacker publishes a malicious npm package with path traversal in tarball file paths.
attack_chain.leads_to: CDNJS automated bot fetches and unpacks the package.

attack_chain.action: CDNJS bot extracts the tarball, ZIP Slip exploit causes files to be written outside the intended directory (e.g., /tmp/ryotak.sh).
attack_chain.leads_to: Malicious files/scripts are placed on the server.

attack_chain.action: Malicious script could be executed or sensitive files could be overwritten, leading to exfiltration of secret API keys and tokens.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker gains access to CDNJS API keys and tokens.

attack_chain.action: With obtained API keys (GITHUB_REPO_API_KEY, WORKERS_KV_API_TOKEN), attacker can tamper with any library or purge/alter CDN cache.
attack_chain.leads_to: Complete compromise of CDNJS infrastructure and supply chain.

behavioral_signatures: Archive extraction with file paths containing '../' or other traversal sequences
Unexpected files appearing outside the intended extraction directory during package ingestion
Automated ingestion processes writing to /tmp or system directories
file_indicators: npm package tarballs with file entries containing '../'
Unexpected shell scripts or files named after package authors in /tmp or other non-package directories
network_indicators: Unusual access to CDNJS API endpoints with newly obtained API keys
Unexpected exfiltration of secrets to external URLs (if attacker script is more advanced)
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor package ingestion pipelines for archive files containing directory traversal in file paths. Block or alert on any extraction attempts that would write files outside the intended package directory. Audit for unexpected files or scripts appearing in system directories during or after package ingestion. Monitor for abnormal use of API keys or tokens, especially those with write or purge permissions.
